<!-- Write for an engineer from another team. Use plain language and established repository terms. Describe observable behavior and concrete evidence; avoid implementation-diary prose, unexplained jargon, generic benefit claims, and private operational context. Delete every placeholder. -->

## Summary

<!-- Write 1–3 bullets describing concrete outcomes: what behavior, interface, or repository surface changed. -->

-

## Why

<!-- Write 2–4 plain sentences. Start with what this component does and who depends on it, then explain what happens today, why that is a problem, and why the change is needed now. Do not repeat the summary. -->

## Linear / Context

<!-- Link the DBU ticket and relevant public pull requests or issues. Write “N/A — exempt” when no ticket is required. -->

-

## Key decisions

<!-- Record only non-obvious decisions. Name the trade-off, what this approach gives up, and why it was chosen. Write “None” when there were no material decisions. -->

-

## Scope / Descoped

<!-- State the boundary of this pull request, including intentionally deferred behavior or follow-up work. -->

-

## Test plan

<!-- List exact commands or manual checks and the result each one verifies. Do not write only “tests pass.” -->

- [ ] Command or check — expected behavior.

## Risk / Rollout

<!-- Describe realistic failure modes, compatibility or migration concerns, rollout order, observability, and rollback where applicable. For a no-runtime-impact change, write “None — documentation/tooling only.” -->
